page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-16GB is a general-purpose virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 4 vCPUs allocated on a shared basis. The CPU operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz and includes 16 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate moderate performance characteristics. The server achieves average ratings in single-core metrics, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 1321.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 7941.3. However, multi-core performance is weaker, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 3006.18 and Geekbench multi-core scoring 3938.0, placing them in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show a stark contrast: small-block cached reads perform at an average rate of 410.01 GB/sec, whereas large-block uncached writes drop to a poor 14.27 GB/sec.

Due to the shared CPU allocation, this server exhibits resource contention tradeoffs, making it less suitable for sustained high-compute workloads like software compilation or ray tracing, which both scored in the bottom 25%. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the shared-resource model offers a budget-friendly entry point for workloads requiring a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio without continuous peak CPU utilization. It is best suited for general-purpose applications, basic web serving, lightweight text and image processing, and small-scale LLM inference tasks.
